extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing reciprocal discipline of a patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice, opportunity to respond, grounds for discipline, findings on failure to respond, suspension period, and publication of a notice of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the suspension of [the Respondent] is ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted state authority. The Notice and Order filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the Supreme Court of California.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: suspension by a duly constituted authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline under § 11.24 may be imposed where the practitioner 'has been suspended on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the state of California' (as stated in the Notice of Suspension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice summarizes the underlying state-court disciplinary findings (e.g., misrepresentation and probation violations) as the factual basis for reciprocal discipline under the cited federal regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1), the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of California.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt number recorded) and delivered; the procedural requirement includes service and an explicit 40-day response window and a specification of permissible bases to oppose reciprocal discipline under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of no response: finding of no genuine issue and imposition of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) suspension of Respondent is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely respond to the Notice and Order may permit the Director to treat the facts as uncontested and to impose the requested reciprocal discipline without a contested hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension period selection and imposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for ninety days starting on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may impose the same period of discipline (here, a 90-day suspension) as imposed by the state authority when ordering reciprocal discipline under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: Official Gazette notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, the practitioner's identity, registration number, the regulatory provisions violated, and a summary of the state-court disciplinary facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a full sample 'Notice of Suspension' showing required elements: practitioner's name and city, registration number, statement that suspension was reciprocal under specific CFR provision, citation to the state order (case number and date), a factual summary of the underlying state disciplinary matters (including specific acts such as misrepresentation and probation noncompliance), statutory citations, and reference to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation as an act involving moral turpitude (Business & Professions Code § 6106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a medical report not authored by the claimed doctor and representing that the report had been prepared by that doctor constitutes an act involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or corruption in willful violation of Business and Professions Code section 6106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice summarizes the state-court stipulation that on December 21, 2009 the Respondent faxed a three-page medical report to the State Bar, misrepresenting the author; such factual misconduct supports ethical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful failure to comply with disciplinary probation conditions (Business & Professions Code § 6068(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to timely comply with the quarterly reporting conditions and the substance abuse conditions of disciplinary probation constitutes failure to comply with all conditions attached to a disciplinary probation in willful violation of Business and Professions Code section 6068(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice recounts that the Supreme Court's disciplinary order imposed probation conditions (quarterly reporting and substance abuse monitoring) and that failure to adhere to those conditions formed a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for action: federal statutory and regulatory citations
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners reference both the USPTO's statutory authority under 35 U.S.C. and the implementing regulations in 37 C.F.R.; practitioners and counsel should cite these authorities in related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service method for Notice and Order (certified mail and proof of delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. 70111150000146353905) and was delivered to Respondent on April 20, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service of the Notice (e.g., certified mail with tracking/receipt) and documentation of delivery are procedural prerequisites to triggering the response period and subsequent reciprocal-discipline process.
